original_value: Bike sharing provides an environment-friendly way for traveling and is booming all over the world. Yet, due to the high similarity of user travel patterns, the bike imbalance problem constantly occurs, especially for dockless bike sharing systems, causing significant impact on service quality and company revenue. Thus, it has become a critical task for bike sharing operators to resolve such imbalance efficiently. In this paper, we propose a novel deep reinforcement learning framework for incentivizing users to rebalance such systems. We model the problem as a Markov decision process and take both spatial and temporal features into consideration. We develop a novel deep reinforcement learning algorithm called Hierarchical Reinforcement Pricing (HRP), which builds upon the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm. Different from existing methods that often ignore spatial information and rely heavily on accurate prediction, HRP captures both spatial and temporal dependencies using a divide-and-conquer structure with an embedded localized module. We conduct extensive experiments to HRP, based on a dataset from Mobike, a major Chinese dockless bike sharing company. Results show that HRP performs close to the 24-timeslot look-ahead optimization, and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both service level and bike distribution. It also transfers well when applied to unseen areas.

result.paraphrase: Bike sharing offers an eco-friendly mode of travel and is rapidly expanding worldwide. However, because users often exhibit highly similar trip patterns, bike imbalance arises repeatedly, especially in dockless bike-sharing systems, which significantly hurts service quality and company revenue. Efficiently addressing this imbalance has therefore become a crucial task for bike-sharing operators. In this paper, we present a new deep reinforcement learning framework to incentivize users to rebalance such systems. We formulate the issue as a Markov decision process and consider both spatial and temporal features. We introduce a novel deep reinforcement learning algorithm, Hierarchical Reinforcement Pricing (HRP), built on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient. Unlike prior approaches that often overlook spatial information and depend heavily on accurate prediction, HRP uses a divide-and-conquer structure with an embedded localized module to capture spatial and temporal dependencies. We perform extensive experiments on HRP using a dataset from Mobike, a major Chinese dockless bike-sharing company. The results indicate that HRP comes close to 24-timeslot look-ahead optimization, surpasses state-of-the-art methods in both service level and bike distribution, and transfers well to unseen areas.
